rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly with no ICE, so this round raises obfuscation pressure across all seven passes while keeping costs bounded for this loop-heavy, template-instantiated numeric benchmark. SUB and BCF get the strongest security/diversity weights because the code is dominated by constant-folded simple-type arithmetic and large straight-line test functions where instruction substitution and bogus predicates add real analysis friction at modest risk. FLA stays high but slightly below BCF since flattening the hot loop-invariant kernels carries the largest runtime exposure. ICALL and IBR are pushed up to disrupt call-graph and control-flow recovery in the many similarly-shaped templated test_variableN instantiations, which also maximizes structural diversity between near-duplicate functions. SPLIT stays moderate as an enabler that improves the efficacy of FLA/BCF on the oversized main (6.7KB) rather than a security pass itself, and IGV remains the lowest-cost complement since globals are sparse in this benchmark. All CorrectnessRisk weights stay at or below 0.25 to preserve the clean correctness record from round 1.
